- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast rise after +10% from recent peak to avoid overshoot.
- If 3+ consecutive days of rising prices with sentiment ≥ 0.5, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust downward by 1–2% in next 2–3 periods.
- If forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
